messages:
jin: Heads up — on the multi-variant canary we just ran I see throughput drop and tail latency regressions. GPU util down ~18%, average batch size collapsed to ~1.8. Feels like compat set fragmentation is killing batching.
sanjay: link to the traces? which variant mix was the canary serving?
jin: https://perf.redwood/capture/1872103208 — traffic was ~60/30/10 between v1,v2,small-quant. Profiler shows a lot of tiny batches and frequent kernel fallback to generic matmul (kernel thrash). snippet from profiler:
```
batch_size_histogram: {1: 42%, 2: 33%, 3: 14%, >=4: 11%}
compat_fragmentation: 0.37
kernel_switch_count: +21% vs baseline
avg_tokens_per_req: 64
```
alex: That compat_fragmentation number is the smoking gun. Two ideas: 1) windowed batch smoothing (hold-for N ms to coalesce across near-compatible variants), 2) soft-compat merging: allow small-cost merges across variants if token_budget impact < X and kernel mismatch penalty low.
alex: Example config sketch:
```
queue_policy:
  max_hold_ms: 5        # short window to smooth arrivals
  soft_compat_threshold: 0.25  # allow merges if estimated perf delta < 25%
  token_budget_target: 512
  compat_penalty_scalar: 0.1
```
lina: Also seeing KV cache cold misses. When soft-compat merges cross model shapes we lose cached KV locality and kernel selection falls back. We should add a prefetech/warmup heuristic: if merging would use same tokenizer/prefix pattern, prefetch KV and prefer kernels matching warmed cache.
lina: quick pseudo-cmd we used to simulate warmup in perf harness:
```bash
# replay top prefixes to warm KV on the node
./perf_run --replay-prefixes top_1k --target-node gpu-17
```
marie: Good. We should measure two metrics: effective batchization (avg batch size & token packing) and kernel stability (kernel-swap/sec). Proposal: run 2x A/B for 4 hours: A = baseline routing, B = windowed smoothing + soft-compat threshold 0.2 + KV warmup prefetch. Use canary on dedicated pool.
sanjay: for routing, we can add a 'batch_score' to routing decisions so fallback/low-priority variants are slightly deprioritized if they reduce batchability. That keeps correctness but nudges traffic into better packing.
jin: Also saw token_budget hits for some sessions — those short-lived high-token requests are starving others. Suggest token_budget_target per-compat-set rather than per-variant; easier to co-allocate across similar models.
alex: Agree. Implementation note: token_budget_target should be adaptive: lower it when queue depth high, raise when idle. We have the telemetry hooks already (queue_depth, avg_wait_ms) — tie target to those signals.
marie: Can we avoid making soft-compat too aggressive? If we merge quantized small models with full-fp ones we might regress quality or exceed mem limits.
alex: Yes — include hard guards: skip merges if model_ram + estimated_kv > node_free_mem or quality_signature_mismatch > threshold.
deploy-bot: canary-restart: canary group "mv-routing-smoothing" restarted at 2028-07-14T12:40:10Z :white_check_mark:
lina: I'll run the KV warmup experiment and collect kernel-switch/sec. Sanjay — can you wire batch_score into multi-variant router for the canary? Jin/Alex — can you land a minimal queue_policy toggle (max_hold_ms + soft_compat_threshold) behind a feature flag?
marie: timeline — experiments tomorrow: KV warmup + router bias + queue_policy toggle. If we get >10% throughput boost or >20% drop in kernel-switch/sec we can promote. Otherwise iterate on hold window or soft threshold.
jin: I'll also add a lightweight logging tag to capture pre/post merge kernel chosen and whether prefetch was used (helps attribution).
alex: I'll draft the perf dashboard widgets: batch_size_dist, kernel_switch_rate, avg_tokens_per_batch, free_mem_by_node.
sanjay: noted. I'll schedule the canary window and create the experiment tracking doc.
marie: Great sync. Keep notes in the canary thread and paste perf links here. :+1:
